name: Aesculus

project_scope.learner_admission: approved Master Plant Pool; both range UNRESOLVED; var. pavia represented by species-level A. pavia

look_here_first: Buckeye identification starts with opposite palmately compound leaves; species separation starts with a mature capsule and the degree of stamen exsertion, not flower color.

comparison.glabra: Usually short-prickly or warty (rarely nearly smooth).

comparison.pavia: Included to barely exserted, roughly petal length.

comparison.glabra: Generally paler greenish-yellow, less tubular; color secondary.
comparison.pavia: Usually red tubular flowers, but var. flavescens yellow; color unreliable.
Opposite, palmately compound, usually 5 (to 7) toothed leaflets; substantial overlap.

cautions: Aesculus × bushii (glabra × pavia) can be intermediate; do not force ID from one trait.
Aesculus pavia var. pavia is an infraspecific source record represented by species-level A. pavia, not an extra card.
Aesculus pavia var. flavescens can be yellow-flowered; do not use color as primary separator.
Both species are Texas-native at state scale in POWO, but target-zone county PASS has not been established.
visual_status: Genus photo-led lesson with five physically verified images; calibrated separating-character pairs pending.

genus_diagnostics.look_here_first: Find OPPOSITE, PALMATELY COMPOUND leaves (several leaflets meeting at one petiole tip). For species ID compare a mature CAPSULE surface and a side-on flower showing STAMENS relative to PETALS.

shared_structure_examples.plain: Five to seven leaflets radiating from one stalk tip.
shared_structure_examples.why: Recognize buckeyes; leaf count overlaps and does not split species.

shared_structure_examples.plain: Branched upright cluster of flowers at the shoot tip.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: whole flower cluster with intact side-view blossoms
shared_structure_examples.why: Shows where to examine stamens and petals.

shared_structure_examples.plain: How far pollen-bearing filaments project beyond petals.
shared_structure_examples.why: Usually strongly projecting in glabra, included or barely projecting in pavia.

shared_structure_examples.plain: Rounded fruit husk enclosing large buckeye seeds.
shared_structure_examples.why: Usually short-warty/prickly in glabra versus smooth in pavia; variation and hybrids require caution.

confusable_genera.distinction: Mexican buckeye has PINNATE leaves with leaflets along a central axis, and a three-valved capsule; Aesculus has palmately compound leaves.
Some maples also have opposite leaves, but Aesculus has palmately compound leaves and rounded capsules, not paired samaras.

teaching_order: Inspect opposite leaf nodes and leaflet attachment
Compare mature capsules at equal scale
Examine stamens relative to petals in side-view flowers
Use habit, buds and range only as supporting context
study_strategy.warning: Flower color and leaflet number overlap; A. pavia var. flavescens may have yellow flowers, and Aesculus × bushii can be intermediate.

comparison_cards.title: Glabra versus pavia: fruit husk
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Inspect several fully mature capsules for short prickles or warts versus a smooth surface.
comparison_cards.difference: Typical A. glabra husks are warty or short-prickly; A. pavia is usually smooth.
comparison_cards.caution: A. glabra can be nearly smooth and hybrid A. × bushii may be intermediate. The current glabra photo shows a finely textured husk, not conspicuous long spines.

comparison_cards.title: Glabra versus pavia: flower side view
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare the length of stamens projecting past the petal tips, not flower color.
comparison_cards.difference: A. glabra often has stamens roughly twice petal length; A. pavia stamens usually near petal length or barely exserted.
comparison_cards.caution: Select similar-stage flowers; one oblique photo is not a measured stamen-to-petal ratio.
